new_ops.name: t5_relative_position_bias
new_ops.reason: The attention op has no additive logit bias. Each head adds a learned scalar to its [T,T] attention logits. The scalar is looked up from a table of 32 buckets indexed by the key-query offset. Bucket ranges grow logarithmically up to an offset of 128, and every larger offset maps to the same bucket. The table is shared across all layers, with a separate value per head. This needs an attention primitive that accepts a per-head [T,T] bias from bucketed relative positions.
new_ops.quote: In this work, we use $32$ embeddings for all of our models with ranges that increase in size logarithmically up to an offset of $128$ beyond which we assign all relative positions to the same embedding.

output.notes: Describes the T5 decoder block for the Base config (the paper's baseline). The encoder block is identical except that its attention is non-causal, and the decoder's cross-attention is omitted from block_ops (see mechanisms_outside_ir). Norm is mapped to rmsnorm from 'only rescaled and no additive bias'. The paper does not say explicitly whether the mean is subtracted. A final norm before the head is not stated, so it is omitted. Several values are left not_stated: q/k/v projection widths (heads*d_kv, not stated as a number), biases, eps, the attention scale, and n_kv_heads. Small's d_kv is not stated. Config order follows the Table 14 caption (Small, Base, Large, 3B, 11B). Primary config is Base because the paper singles it out as its baseline.
